newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks hit closing and intraday highs.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks hit closing and intraday highs.

text.p: Toronto stocks soared to new heights on Tuesday, led by a gold rally as bargain hunters snapped up precious metal stocks, analysts said.
The TSE 300 Index jumped 38.48 points to close at 5329.55 in turnover of 82.6 million shares valued at C$1.23 billion (US$905 million).
The key index also set a new intra-day high of 5332.02, surpassing the previous record set on September 26.

"Gold is up and the bonds remain quite strong. You put that together with inflation growing at a modest pace and it's an exciting market," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser with Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd.
Gold stocks were pounded on Monday as COMEX gold futures suffered heavy losses. COMEX prices rebounded slightly today with December gold ending up US$0.50 at US$381.00 an ounce.
A Canadian bond rally on the back of gains in U.S. treasury also pulled Toronto equities higher.
Canada's 9.00 percent bond closed up 0.70 at C$104.15 to yield 7.632 percent. Bond traders said both Canadian and U.S. markets were aided by weaker-than-expected U.S. economic data.
The TSE moved ahead in 111 of 14 sub-groups. Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 498 to 394 with 291 issues flat.
* Among gold stocks, Placer Dome Inc. rose 0.25 to 32.45 on 1.4 million shares. Barrick Gold Corp. jumped 1.20 to 35.25 on 1.6 million shares.
After markets closed, Barrick said it will not proceed with its Cerro Corona project in Peru. Barrick also said it will take a C$38 million (US$28 million) charge to third quarter earnings.
* Onex Corp. closed up 0.50 at 14.65 on 47,000 shares after announcing plans to acquire an electronics unit from IBM Canada for C$750 million (US$551 million).
* CAE Inc. topped the most-active list, adding 0.05 to 10.50 on 2.4 million shares.
